subject: Computer Science
title: Computer and Its Characteristics
summary: This chapter introduces the computer, its origin from the Latin word 'computare' (to compute/calculate), and its main characteristics: speed (millions of calculations per second), accuracy (near 100%, GIGO principle), automation (works automatically after input), diligence (works continuously without fatigue), versatility (handles different tasks via different programs), and storage capacity (measured in bits/bytes: 1 nibble = 4 bits, 1 byte = 8 bits, KB = 1024 bytes).

concepts.text: An electronic machine that accepts data, processes it according to instructions, and produces output.
Garbage In Garbage Out — incorrect input gives incorrect output; correct input gives correct output.
1 bit = 0/1; 4 bits = 1 nibble; 8 bits = 1 byte; 1024 bytes = 1 KB; 1024 KB = 1 MB.
Same computer can do math calculations, graphics design, word processing, and programming depending on the software provided.

very_short.q: From which Latin word is the term 'computer' derived?
Give any two examples of input devices.
Name any two permanent storage devices.
very_short.a: Hard disk and USB flash drive (or CD/DVD).
Garbage In Garbage Out — wrong input produces wrong output.

short.a: A computer is diligent because it can perform repetitive tasks continuously for hours or days without becoming bored or tired, maintaining the same speed and accuracy.
A computer can perform different tasks (simple calculations to complex logic) depending on the program provided. It is not limited to one type of job.
Accuracy is consistently high (about 100%). It depends on correct input and instructions. The GIGO principle states incorrect input leads to incorrect output.

long.q: Describe the major characteristics of a computer.
long.a: The major characteristics are: (1) Speed — millions of calculations per second; (2) Accuracy — ~100% if input is correct (GIGO); (3) Automation — works automatically after receiving data and instructions; (4) Diligence — performs repetitive tasks continuously without fatigue; (5) Versatility — handles different jobs using different programs; (6) Storage capacity — stores huge amounts in memory divided into primary (RAM/ROM) and secondary (disk/USB/CD).

exercise.q: 1. From which Latin word is the term 'computer' derived? Explain.
exercise.a: The term is derived from the Latin word 'computare', meaning 'to calculate' or 'to compute'.

exercise.q: 2. What does CPU stand for? What is its role?
exercise.a: CPU = Central Processing Unit. It is the brain of the computer that processes instructions and performs calculations.

exercise.q: 3. Give any two examples of input devices.
exercise.a: Keyboard and mouse are common input devices.

exercise.q: 4. Name any two permanent storage devices.
exercise.a: Hard disk drive and USB flash drive are permanent (secondary) storage devices.
Diligence means a computer can work continuously for long periods without becoming tired or bored, repeating tasks with the same speed and accuracy.

exercise.q: Self-Test 1.1 — 2. What does GIGO stand for?
Self-Test 1.1 — 3. What do you mean by versatility?
exercise.a: Versatility means the computer can perform many different types of tasks depending on the program given to it.

exercise.q: Self-Test 1.1 — 4. What do you mean by accuracy?
exercise.a: Accuracy means the computer produces correct results (near 100%) when given correct input and instructions.

study_note: Remember: Computer = input → process → output. Key traits: Speed, Accuracy (GIGO), Automation, Diligence, Versatility, Storage. Units: bit → nibble → byte → KB → MB.
